request.spec:
Periods can be generated: a from-date and a to-date and a button create one period per calendar
month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, each running from the first to the last
day of its month (February ends on the 28th or 29th), named yyyy-mm, each written as PERIOD_ADDED.
A month whose name is already a period, or whose days overlap a period on the sheet, is left out
and the others are still made. Show how many were made. A to-date before the from-date is refused
with an error.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Periods can be generated: a from-date and a to-date and a button create one period per calendar
month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, each running from the first to the last
day of its month (February ends on the 28th or 29th), named yyyy-mm, each written as PERIOD_ADDED.
A month whose name is already a period, or whose days overlap a period on the sheet, is left out
and the others are still made. Show how many were made. A to-date before the from-date is refused
with an error.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
You can now generate monthly periods on a sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**How it works:** the Periods section has a new form with a from-date, a to-date and a "Generate monthly periods" button. It makes one period for each calendar month from the from-date's month through the to-date's month. Each runs from the 1st to the last day of its month (February ends on the 28th or 29th), is named `yyyy-mm`, and writes a `PERIOD_ADDED` record to the audit file. Afterwards the form shows how many were made.

**What gets skipped:** a month is left out if a period with that name already exists (case ignored) or if its days overlap an existing period. The other months are still made. For example, with a period `P1` from 2026-03-05 to 03-08, generating from 2026-02-15 to 2026-04-10 makes `2026-02` and `2026-04` and skips March.

**Refusals:** a to-date before the from-date is refused with an error and nothing is created. A blank from-date uses the sheet's today, as the other forms do.

**Code changes:**
- **Server:** a new `PeriodService.generate` method and a `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate` endpoint. It locks the sheet the same way adding a single period does, so two people generating at the same time can't create overlapping periods.
- **Front end:** the generate form is in `features/periods/periods.ts`, using the test IDs the spec expects (`period-generate-from`, `period-generate-to`, `period-generate`, `period-generated`, `period-generate-error`).
- **Database:** no schema change was needed, because generated periods are stored like any other period.
